# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Complete dataset revision import into the customer's original Rails database.
require "active_record"
require "active_support/time"
require "set"
require "date"
require "time"
require "csv"
require_relative "dataset_delivery"

module Starforge
  class RailsDataset
    SCHEMA = "stellar-forge.rails-dataset-import.v1"
    TYPES = %w[string integer decimal boolean date datetime].freeze

    class ImportError < StandardError
      attr_reader :code, :details
      def initialize(code, **details)
        @code, @details = code, details
        super([code, details.map { |key,value| "#{key}=#{value.inspect}" }.join(" ")].reject(&:empty?).join(": "))
      end
    end

    def self.need(condition, code, **details)
      raise ImportError.new(code, **details) unless condition
    end

    # Tagged values preserve native integers, decimal precision and dates in
    # complete previews/receipts without JSON's binary-number conversions.
    def self.pack(value)
      case value
      when NilClass then ["null"]
      when TrueClass, FalseClass then ["boolean", value]
      when String then ["string", value]
      when Integer then ["integer", value.to_s]
      when BigDecimal
        need(value.finite?, "DATASET_FINITE_DECIMAL")
        ["decimal", value.to_s("F")]
      when ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, Time, DateTime then ["datetime", value.to_time.utc.iso8601(9)]
      when Date then ["date", value.iso8601]
      when Array then ["array", value.map { |item| pack(item) }]
      when Hash
        need(value.keys.all? { |key| key.is_a?(String) }, "DATASET_STRING_KEYS")
        ["object", value.keys.sort.map { |key| [key, pack(value.fetch(key))] }]
      else
        raise ImportError.new("DATASET_EXACT_VALUE", type: value.class.name)
      end
    end

    def self.unpack(value)
      type, data = value
      case type
      when "null" then nil
      when "boolean", "string" then data
      when "integer" then Integer(data, 10)
      when "decimal" then BigDecimal(data)
      when "date" then Date.iso8601(data)
      when "datetime" then Time.iso8601(data)
      when "array" then data.map { |item| unpack(item) }
      when "object" then data.to_h { |key,item| [key, unpack(item)] }
      else raise ImportError.new("DATASET_TAGGED_VALUE")
      end
    end

    def self.json(value)
      JSON.generate(value, allow_nan: false, max_nesting: 100)
    end

    def self.exact_json(value)
      json(pack(value))
    end

    def self.sha(value)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(value.b)
    end

    def self.fingerprint(value)
      sha(exact_json(value))
    end

    def self.copy_json(value)
      JSON.parse(json(value), create_additions: false, allow_nan: false)
    end

    # The complete original source is streamed into a private preview, then
    # streamed again when reviewed or committed. Only key identities stay in RAM.
    class Preview
      attr_reader :binding, :counts, :sha256, :entries_sha256, :row_count
      def initialize(binding)
        @binding = RailsDataset.copy_json(binding)
        @counts = {"inserted"=>0, "updated"=>0, "unchanged"=>0, "removed"=>0,
                   "adopted"=>0, "restored"=>0, "source_changed"=>0}
        @file = Tempfile.new(["starforge-dataset-preview-", ".jsonl"])
        @file.binmode
        @file.unlink
        @digest, @row_count, @sealed, @closed = Digest::SHA256.new, 0, false, false
      end

      def append(entry)
        RailsDataset.need(!@sealed && !@closed, "DATASET_PREVIEW_SEALED")
        raw = RailsDataset.json(entry) + "\n"
        @file.write(raw)
        @digest.update(raw)
        @row_count += 1
        @counts.fetch(entry.fetch("action"))
        @counts[entry.fetch("action")] += 1
        %w[adopted restored source_changed].each { |key| @counts[key] += 1 if entry[key] }
      end

      def seal
        RailsDataset.need(!@closed, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CLOSED")
        unless @sealed
          @file.flush
          @entries_sha256 = @digest.hexdigest
          @sha256 = RailsDataset.fingerprint({"schema"=>SCHEMA, "binding"=>@binding,
            "counts"=>@counts, "row_count"=>@row_count, "entries_sha256"=>@entries_sha256})
          DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@binding)
          DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@counts)
          @sha256.freeze
          @entries_sha256.freeze
          @sealed = true
        end
        self
      end

      def each_entry
        return enum_for(__method__) unless block_given?
        RailsDataset.need(@sealed && !@closed, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CLOSED")
        @file.rewind
        seen = Digest::SHA256.new
        @file.each_line do |line|
          seen.update(line)
          yield JSON.parse(line, create_additions: false, allow_nan: false)
        end
        RailsDataset.need(seen.hexdigest == @entries_sha256, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CHANGED")
        self
      end

      def summary
        RailsDataset.need(@sealed && !@closed, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CLOSED")
        {"schema"=>SCHEMA, "binding"=>RailsDataset.copy_json(@binding),
         "preview_sha256"=>@sha256, "entries_sha256"=>@entries_sha256,
         "row_count"=>@row_count, "counts"=>@counts.dup}
      end

      def write_json(io)
        header = RailsDataset.json(summary)
        io.write(header.delete_suffix("}") + ',"rows":[')
        first = true
        each_entry do |row|
          io.write(",") unless first
          io.write(RailsDataset.json(row))
          first = false
        end
        io.write("]}\n")
        self
      end

      def write_csv(io)
        csv = CSV.new(io, force_quotes: true, row_sep: "\n")
        csv << %w[action source_ordinal key target_id adopted restored source_changed before after original_source_json source_row_sha256]
        each_entry do |row|
          csv << [row["action"], row["source_ordinal"], row["key_json"], row["target_id"],
            row["adopted"], row["restored"], row["source_changed"],
            row["before_json"], row["after_json"], row["source_raw_json"], row["source_row_sha256"]]
        end
        csv.flush
        self
      end

      def close
        return if @closed
        @closed = true
        @file.close
      end
    end

    # Explicit field mapping; a missing field can be preserved, while a supplied
    # null can independently be assigned or preserved. Keys always need values.
    class Mapping
      attr_reader :definition, :columns, :key_columns, :sha256, :key_sha256, :removal
      def initialize(definition, model, fields, protected_columns)
        RailsDataset.need(definition.is_a?(Hash), "DATASET_MAPPING")
        @definition = RailsDataset.copy_json(definition)
        RailsDataset.need(@definition["schema"] == "stellar-forge.rails-dataset-mapping.v1",
          "DATASET_MAPPING_SCHEMA")
        @columns, @key_columns = @definition["columns"], @definition["key_columns"]
        RailsDataset.need(@columns.is_a?(Hash) && !@columns.empty? &&
          @key_columns.is_a?(Array) && !@key_columns.empty? &&
          @key_columns.uniq == @key_columns && @key_columns.all? { |key| key.is_a?(String) && @columns.key?(key) },
          "DATASET_MAPPING_KEYS")
        @model = model
        @columns.each do |name,spec|
          RailsDataset.need(name.is_a?(String) && model.columns_hash.key?(name) &&
            !protected_columns.include?(name), "DATASET_TARGET_COLUMN", column: name)
          RailsDataset.need(spec.is_a?(Hash) && fields.include?(spec["field"]) &&
            TYPES.include?(spec["type"]) && %w[assign preserve].include?(spec.fetch("null", "assign")) &&
            %w[error preserve].include?(spec.fetch("missing", "error")) &&
            [true,false].include?(spec.fetch("stringify", false)), "DATASET_FIELD_MAPPING", column: name)
          RailsDataset.need((spec.keys - %w[field type null missing stringify]).empty?,
            "DATASET_MAPPING_OPTION", column: name)
          RailsDataset.need(!@key_columns.include?(name) ||
            (spec.fetch("null", "assign") == "assign" && spec.fetch("missing", "error") == "error"),
            "DATASET_KEY_REQUIRED", column: name)
          verify_type(name, spec["type"])
        end
        @removal = @definition.fetch("removal", {"strategy"=>"retain"})
        RailsDataset.need(@removal.is_a?(Hash) && %w[retain archive].include?(@removal["strategy"]),
          "DATASET_REMOVAL_POLICY")
        allowed_removal = @removal["strategy"] == "archive" ? %w[strategy column active inactive] : %w[strategy]
        RailsDataset.need((@removal.keys - allowed_removal).empty?, "DATASET_REMOVAL_OPTION")
        if @removal["strategy"] == "archive"
          name = @removal["column"]
          RailsDataset.need(name.is_a?(String) && model.columns_hash.key?(name) &&
            model.type_for_attribute(name).type == :boolean &&
            !protected_columns.include?(name) && !@columns.key?(name),
            "DATASET_ARCHIVE_COLUMN")
          RailsDataset.need(@removal.fetch("active", true) == true && @removal.fetch("inactive", false) == false,
            "DATASET_ARCHIVE_BOOLEAN")
        end
        RailsDataset.need((@definition.keys - %w[schema columns key_columns removal]).empty?,
          "DATASET_MAPPING_OPTION")
        DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@definition)
        DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@removal)
        @sha256 = RailsDataset.fingerprint(@definition).freeze
        @key_sha256 = RailsDataset.fingerprint({"key_columns"=>@key_columns,
          "columns"=>@columns.slice(*@key_columns)}).freeze
      end

      def verify_type(name, type)
        actual = @model.type_for_attribute(name).type
        accepted = {"string"=>[:string,:text], "integer"=>[:integer],
          "decimal"=>[:decimal], "boolean"=>[:boolean], "date"=>[:date],
          "datetime"=>[:datetime,:timestamp]}
        RailsDataset.need(accepted.fetch(type).include?(actual), "DATASET_COLUMN_TYPE",
          column: name, declared: type, actual: actual)
      end

      def converted(name, spec, value)
        if value.nil?
          RailsDataset.need(@model.columns_hash.fetch(name).null, "DATASET_COLUMN_NULL", column: name)
          return nil
        end
        selected = case spec["type"]
        when "string"
          if value.is_a?(String)
            value
          elsif spec["stringify"] && (value.is_a?(Integer) || value.is_a?(BigDecimal) || value == true || value == false)
            value.is_a?(BigDecimal) ? value.to_s("F") : value.to_s
          else
            raise ImportError.new("DATASET_TEXT_REQUIRED", column: name)
          end
        when "integer"
          if value.is_a?(Integer)
            value
          elsif value.is_a?(BigDecimal) && value.finite? && value.frac.zero?
            value.to_i
          elsif value.is_a?(String) && /\A[+-]?[0-9]+\z/.match?(value)
            Integer(value, 10)
          else
            raise ImportError.new("DATASET_INTEGER_REQUIRED", column: name)
          end
        when "decimal"
          RailsDataset.need(value.is_a?(Integer) || value.is_a?(BigDecimal) ||
            value.is_a?(String) && /\A[+-]?(?:[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]*)?|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?\z/.match?(value),
            "DATASET_DECIMAL_REQUIRED", column: name)
          parsed = value.is_a?(BigDecimal) ? value : BigDecimal(value.to_s)
          RailsDataset.need(parsed.finite?, "DATASET_FINITE_DECIMAL", column: name)
          parsed
        when "boolean"
          RailsDataset.need(value == true || value == false, "DATASET_BOOLEAN_REQUIRED", column: name)
          value
        when "date"
          RailsDataset.need(value.is_a?(String) && /\A[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\z/.match?(value),
            "DATASET_DATE_REQUIRED", column: name)
          Date.iso8601(value)
        when "datetime"
          RailsDataset.need(value.is_a?(String) &&
            /\A[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T.+(?:Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})\z/.match?(value),
            "DATASET_TIMESTAMP_OFFSET", column: name)
          Time.iso8601(value).utc
        end
        if selected.is_a?(String)
          RailsDataset.need(selected.valid_encoding? && !selected.include?("\0"), "DATASET_TEXT_ENCODING", column: name)
          limit = @model.columns_hash.fetch(name).limit
          RailsDataset.need(limit.nil? || selected.length <= limit, "DATASET_TEXT_LENGTH", column: name)
        end
        if selected.is_a?(BigDecimal)
          column = @model.columns_hash.fetch(name)
          if column.precision && column.scale
            integral_digits = selected.zero? ? 0 : [selected.abs.exponent, 0].max
            RailsDataset.need(integral_digits <= column.precision - column.scale,
              "DATASET_DECIMAL_RANGE", column: name, precision: column.precision, scale: column.scale)
          end
        end
        type = @model.type_for_attribute(name)
        returned = type.deserialize(type.serialize(selected))
        RailsDataset.need(returned == selected, "DATASET_COLUMN_PRECISION", column: name,
          selected: selected.to_s, stored: returned.to_s)
        selected
      rescue ArgumentError, RangeError => error
        raise ImportError.new("DATASET_COLUMN_VALUE", column: name, reason: error.message)
      end

      def values(row)
        RailsDataset.need(row.is_a?(Hash), "DATASET_SOURCE_ROW")
        result = {}
        @columns.each do |name,spec|
          field = spec.fetch("field")
          unless row.key?(field)
            RailsDataset.need(spec.fetch("missing", "error") == "preserve",
              "DATASET_SOURCE_FIELD_MISSING", field: field)
            next
          end
          next if row[field].nil? && spec.fetch("null", "assign") == "preserve"
          result[name] = converted(name, spec, row[field])
        end
        @key_columns.each do |name|
          value = result[name]
          RailsDataset.need(!value.nil? && !(value.is_a?(String) && value.empty?),
            "DATASET_KEY_REQUIRED", column: name)
        end
        result[@removal["column"]] = true if @removal["strategy"] == "archive"
        result
      end

      def key(values)
        selected = @key_columns.to_h { |name| [name, values.fetch(name)] }
        raw = RailsDataset.exact_json(selected)
        [RailsDataset.sha(raw), raw]
      end

      def removed_values
        @removal["strategy"] == "archive" ? {@removal.fetch("column")=>false} : {}
      end

      def target_columns
        (@columns.keys + (@removal["strategy"] == "archive" ? [@removal["column"]] : [])).uniq
      end
    end

    attr_reader :mapping

    # models contains the application's edition, row and entry ActiveRecord
    # classes. stream is its persisted stream record; scope is its authorized
    # tenant relation. Every model must use the very same database connection.
    def initialize(delivery:, scope:, stream:, models:, mapping:)
      self.class.need(delivery.is_a?(DatasetDelivery), "DATASET_ORIGINAL_DELIVERY")
      self.class.need(scope.is_a?(ActiveRecord::Relation) && stream.is_a?(ActiveRecord::Base) &&
        stream.persisted?, "DATASET_NATIVE_SCOPE")
      self.class.need(models.is_a?(Hash) && %i[edition row entry].all? { |key|
        models[key].is_a?(Class) && models[key] < ActiveRecord::Base }, "DATASET_NATIVE_MODELS")
      @delivery, @scope, @stream = delivery, scope.reorder(nil), stream
      @model, @models = @scope.klass, models.slice(:edition, :row, :entry).freeze
      self.class.need(@scope.limit_value.nil? && @scope.offset_value.nil? &&
        @scope.group_values.empty?, "DATASET_COMPLETE_TARGET_SCOPE")
      pool = @stream.class.connection_pool
      self.class.need(([@model] + @models.values).all? { |model| model.connection_pool.equal?(pool) },
        "DATASET_ONE_DATABASE")
      self.class.need(@model.primary_key.is_a?(String), "DATASET_TARGET_PRIMARY_KEY")
      @pk = @model.primary_key
      @scope_values = @scope.scope_for_create.stringify_keys
      protected_columns = ([@pk, @model.inheritance_column, "created_at", "updated_at", "lock_version"] +
        @scope_values.keys).compact.uniq
      @mapping = Mapping.new(mapping, @model, @delivery.fields, protected_columns)
      @scope_sha = self.class.fingerprint({"model"=>@model.name, "sql"=>@scope.to_sql,
        "creation_values"=>@scope_values})
      @membership = self.class.copy_json(@delivery.membership)
      self.class.need(@membership.is_a?(Hash) &&
        @membership["query_sha256"].is_a?(String) &&
        /\A[a-f0-9]{64}\z/.match?(@membership["query_sha256"]) &&
        @membership["projected_fields"] == @delivery.fields, "DATASET_QUERY_MEMBERSHIP")
      DatasetDelivery.freeze_value(@membership)
      @membership_sha = self.class.fingerprint(@membership)
      @schema_sha = self.class.fingerprint(@mapping.target_columns.sort.map do |name|
        column = @model.columns_hash.fetch(name)
        {"name"=>name, "type"=>column.type.to_s, "sql_type"=>column.sql_type,
         "limit"=>column.limit, "precision"=>column.precision, "scale"=>column.scale, "null"=>column.null}
      end)
      verify_unique_key!
    end

    def verify_unique_key!
      allowed = (@mapping.key_columns + @scope_values.keys).uniq
      indexes = @model.connection.indexes(@model.table_name)
      eligible = indexes.any? do |index|
        columns = index.columns
        index.unique && columns.is_a?(Array) &&
          (@mapping.key_columns - columns).empty? && (columns - allowed).empty? &&
          (!index.respond_to?(:where) || index.where.nil? || index.where.empty?)
      end
      self.class.need(eligible, "DATASET_UNIQUE_TARGET_KEY",
        columns: @mapping.key_columns, scope_columns: @scope_values.keys)
    end

    def validate_stream!
      {"target_model"=>@model.name, "scope_sha256"=>@scope_sha,
       "key_mapping_sha256"=>@mapping.key_sha256, "membership_sha256"=>@membership_sha}.each do |key,expected|
        actual = @stream.public_send(key)
        self.class.need(actual.nil? || actual == expected, "DATASET_STREAM_BINDING", field: key)
      end
      self.class.need(@stream.revision.is_a?(Integer) && @stream.revision >= 0, "DATASET_STREAM_REVISION")
    end

    def source_binding
      {"manifest_sha256"=>@delivery.manifest_sha256, "source_sha256"=>@delivery.source_sha256,
       "snapshot"=>self.class.pack(@delivery.snapshot), "row_count"=>@delivery.row_count,
       "fields"=>@delivery.fields, "membership"=>@membership}
    end

    def prior_receipt
      return nil if @stream.latest_edition_id.nil?
      edition = @models[:edition].find_by(id: @stream.latest_edition_id, dataset_stream_id: @stream.id)
      self.class.need(edition, "DATASET_PRIOR_EDITION_MISSING")
      verified_receipt(edition)
      self.class.need(edition.revision == @stream.revision, "DATASET_PRIOR_REVISION_CHANGED")
      edition.receipt_sha256
    end

    def binding
      validate_stream!
      {"stream_id"=>@stream.id.to_s, "target_model"=>@model.name, "scope_sha256"=>@scope_sha,
       "source"=>source_binding, "mapping"=>@mapping.definition, "mapping_sha256"=>@mapping.sha256,
       "schema_sha256"=>@schema_sha, "prior_revision"=>@stream.revision,
       "prior_edition_id"=>@stream.latest_edition_id&.to_s, "prior_receipt_sha256"=>prior_receipt}
    end

    def preview
      result = nil
      @stream.with_lock { result = build_preview }
      result
    end

    def key_tuple(record)
      @mapping.key_columns.to_h { |name| [name, record.public_send(name)] }
    end

    def target_values(record, columns)
      return {} unless record
      columns.to_h { |name| [name, record.public_send(name)] }
    end

    def target_fingerprint(record, columns)
      values = {"present"=>!record.nil?, "id"=>record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s,
        "values"=>target_values(record, columns)}
      values["lock_version"] = record.lock_version if record && record.has_attribute?("lock_version")
      self.class.fingerprint(values)
    end

    def matching_targets(batch)
      table = @model.arel_table
      predicates = batch.map do |row|
        @mapping.key_columns.map { |name| table[name].eq(row.fetch("values").fetch(name)) }.reduce(&:and)
      end
      return {} if predicates.empty?
      @scope.where(predicates.reduce(&:or)).lock.to_a.group_by do |record|
        @mapping.key(key_tuple(record)).first
      end
    end

    def append_incoming(plan, batch, seen_targets)
      states = @models[:row].where(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id,
        key_sha256: batch.map { |row| row["key_sha256"] }).to_a.index_by(&:key_sha256)
      ids = states.values.map(&:target_id).compact
      tracked = ids.empty? ? {} : @scope.where(@pk=>ids).lock.to_a.index_by { |record| record.public_send(@pk).to_s }
      missing_ids = ids.map(&:to_s) - tracked.keys
      if !missing_ids.empty? && @model.unscoped.where(@pk=>missing_ids).exists?
        raise ImportError.new("DATASET_MANAGED_TARGET_OUTSIDE_SCOPE")
      end
      candidates = matching_targets(batch)
      selected = batch.map do |row|
        state = states[row["key_sha256"]]
        original = state && tracked[state.target_id.to_s]
        found = candidates.fetch(row["key_sha256"], [])
        found = ([original] + found).compact.uniq { |record| record.public_send(@pk).to_s }
        self.class.need(found.length <= 1, "DATASET_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS", key: row["key_json"])
        [row, state, found.first]
      end
      target_ids = selected.map { |_,_,record| record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s }.compact
      owners = @models[:row].where(target_model: @model.name, target_id: target_ids).to_a
        .index_by { |row| row.target_id.to_s }
      selected.each do |row,state,record|
        target_id = record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s
        if target_id
          self.class.need(seen_targets.add?(target_id), "DATASET_TARGET_REUSED", target_id: target_id)
          owner = owners[target_id]
          self.class.need(owner.nil? || (owner.dataset_stream_id.to_s == @stream.id.to_s &&
            owner.key_sha256 == row["key_sha256"]), "DATASET_TARGET_ALREADY_MANAGED", target_id: target_id)
        end
        columns = row.fetch("values").keys
        before = target_values(record, columns)
        changed = !record || before != row["values"]
        action = !record ? "inserted" : changed ? "updated" : "unchanged"
        plan.append(row.except("values").merge(
          "action"=>action, "target_id"=>target_id, "state_id"=>state&.id&.to_s,
          "adopted"=>state.nil? && !record.nil?, "restored"=>state && state.status == "removed",
          "source_changed"=>state && state.source_row_sha256 != row["source_row_sha256"],
          "before_json"=>self.class.exact_json(before), "after_json"=>self.class.exact_json(row["values"]),
          "target_fingerprint"=>target_fingerprint(record, columns)))
      end
    end

    def append_removed(plan, seen_keys)
      @models[:row].where(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, status: "active").in_batches(of: 200) do |relation|
        states = relation.to_a.reject { |row| seen_keys.include?(row.key_sha256) }
        ids = states.map(&:target_id).compact
        targets = ids.empty? ? {} : @scope.where(@pk=>ids).lock.to_a.index_by { |record| record.public_send(@pk).to_s }
        states.sort_by(&:key_sha256).each do |state|
          record = targets[state.target_id.to_s]
          if record.nil? && state.target_id && @model.unscoped.where(@pk=>state.target_id).exists?
            raise ImportError.new("DATASET_MANAGED_TARGET_OUTSIDE_SCOPE")
          end
          values = @mapping.removed_values
          plan.append({"action"=>"removed", "key_sha256"=>state.key_sha256, "key_json"=>state.key_json,
            "target_id"=>record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s, "previous_target_id"=>state.target_id,
            "state_id"=>state.id.to_s, "source_ordinal"=>nil, "source_raw_json"=>nil,
            "source_row_sha256"=>nil, "adopted"=>false, "restored"=>false, "source_changed"=>false,
            "before_json"=>self.class.exact_json(target_values(record, values.keys)),
            "after_json"=>self.class.exact_json(values),
            "target_fingerprint"=>target_fingerprint(record, values.keys)})
        end
      end
    end

    def build_preview
      plan = Preview.new(binding)
      seen_keys, seen_targets, ordinal = Set.new, Set.new, 0
      # Keep SQL parameter counts practical without limiting the complete dataset.
      batch_size = [200, [800 / @mapping.key_columns.length, 1].max].min
      @delivery.each_record.each_slice(batch_size) do |records|
        selected = records.map do |record|
          self.class.need(record["ordinal"] == ordinal && record["raw_json"].is_a?(String) &&
            self.class.sha(record["raw_json"]) == record["sha256"], "DATASET_ORIGINAL_ROW", ordinal: ordinal)
          values = @mapping.values(record.fetch("values"))
          key_sha, key_json = @mapping.key(values)
          self.class.need(seen_keys.add?(key_sha), "DATASET_DUPLICATE_SOURCE_KEY", ordinal: ordinal, key: key_json)
          row = {"key_sha256"=>key_sha, "key_json"=>key_json, "values"=>values,
            "source_ordinal"=>ordinal, "source_raw_json"=>record["raw_json"], "source_row_sha256"=>record["sha256"]}
          ordinal += 1
          row
        end
        append_incoming(plan, selected, seen_targets)
      end
      self.class.need(ordinal == @delivery.row_count, "DATASET_COMPLETE_ROWS",
        actual: ordinal, declared: @delivery.row_count)
      append_removed(plan, seen_keys)
      plan.seal
    rescue Exception
      plan&.close
      raise
    end

    def verified_receipt(edition)
      raw = edition.receipt_json
      self.class.need(raw.is_a?(String) && self.class.sha(raw) == edition.receipt_sha256,
        "DATASET_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
      receipt = JSON.parse(raw, create_additions: false, allow_nan: false)
      self.class.need(receipt["schema"] == SCHEMA &&
        receipt["stream_id"] == @stream.id.to_s && receipt["edition_id"] == edition.id.to_s &&
        receipt["revision"] == edition.revision && receipt["operation_sha256"] == edition.operation_sha256 &&
        receipt["manifest_sha256"] == edition.manifest_sha256 &&
        receipt["source_sha256"] == edition.source_sha256 && receipt["mapping_sha256"] == edition.mapping_sha256 &&
        receipt["binding"] == JSON.parse(edition.binding_json) &&
        receipt["preview_sha256"] == edition.preview_sha256, "DATASET_RECEIPT_BINDING")
      receipt
    end

    def receipt(operation_key:)
      operation_sha = operation_identity(operation_key)
      edition = @models[:edition].find_by(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, operation_sha256: operation_sha)
      self.class.need(edition, "DATASET_RECEIPT_MISSING")
      validate_stream!
      verified_receipt(edition)
    end

    def operation_identity(value)
      self.class.need(value.is_a?(String) && value.valid_encoding? && !value.strip.empty? &&
        value.bytesize <= 1024, "DATASET_OPERATION_KEY")
      self.class.sha(value)
    end

    def apply_entry(entry, edition)
      values = self.class.unpack(JSON.parse(entry.fetch("after_json")))
      record = entry["target_id"] && @scope.lock.find_by(@pk=>entry["target_id"])
      self.class.need(target_fingerprint(record, values.keys) == entry["target_fingerprint"],
        "DATASET_TARGET_CHANGED", key: entry["key_json"])
      if entry["action"] == "inserted"
        record = @scope.new(values)
        self.class.need(record.save!, "DATASET_MODEL_SAVE")
      elsif record && entry["action"] != "unchanged" && !values.empty?
        record.assign_attributes(values)
        self.class.need(record.save!, "DATASET_MODEL_SAVE")
      end
      if record
        record.reload
        self.class.need(@scope.where(@pk=>record.public_send(@pk)).exists?, "DATASET_TARGET_SCOPE_CHANGED")
        self.class.need(target_values(record, values.keys) == values,
          "DATASET_STORED_VALUES_CHANGED", key: entry["key_json"])
      end
      target_id = record&.public_send(@pk)&.to_s || entry["previous_target_id"]
      state = @models[:row].find_or_initialize_by(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, key_sha256: entry["key_sha256"])
      self.class.need(state.new_record? || state.id.to_s == entry["state_id"], "DATASET_KEY_STATE_CHANGED")
      state.assign_attributes(key_json: entry["key_json"], target_model: @model.name, target_id: target_id,
        status: entry["action"] == "removed" ? "removed" : "active", last_edition_id: edition.id)
      unless entry["action"] == "removed"
        state.source_row_sha256 = entry["source_row_sha256"]
        state.values_json = entry["after_json"]
      end
      expected_state = state.attributes.slice("dataset_stream_id", "key_sha256", "key_json", "target_model",
        "target_id", "status", "last_edition_id", "source_row_sha256", "values_json")
      self.class.need(state.save!, "DATASET_KEY_STATE_SAVE")
      self.class.need(state.reload.attributes.slice(*expected_state.keys) == expected_state,
        "DATASET_KEY_STATE_WRITE_CHANGED")
      stored = entry.merge("target_id"=>target_id, "edition_id"=>edition.id.to_s)
      raw = self.class.json(stored)
      @models[:entry].create!(dataset_edition_id: edition.id, key_sha256: entry["key_sha256"],
        source_ordinal: entry["source_ordinal"], action: entry["action"], target_id: target_id,
        record_json: raw, record_sha256: self.class.sha(raw))
      stored
    end

    def import!(operation_key:, expected_preview_sha256:)
      self.class.need(expected_preview_sha256.is_a?(String) &&
        /\A[a-f0-9]{64}\z/.match?(expected_preview_sha256), "DATASET_SELECTED_PREVIEW")
      self.class.need(!@stream.class.connection.transaction_open?, "DATASET_IMPORT_TRANSACTION",
        reason: "Call the importer as the job's database transaction boundary.")
      operation_sha = operation_identity(operation_key)
      result, plan = nil, nil
      @stream.with_lock do
        validate_stream!
        existing = @models[:edition].find_by(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, operation_sha256: operation_sha)
        if existing
          self.class.need(existing.manifest_sha256 == @delivery.manifest_sha256 &&
            existing.mapping_sha256 == @mapping.sha256 && existing.preview_sha256 == expected_preview_sha256,
            "DATASET_OPERATION_CHANGED")
          result = verified_receipt(existing)
        else
          plan = build_preview
          self.class.need(plan.sha256 == expected_preview_sha256, "DATASET_PREVIEW_CHANGED",
            expected: expected_preview_sha256, current: plan.sha256)
          revision = @stream.revision + 1
          edition = @models[:edition].create!(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, revision: revision,
            operation_sha256: operation_sha, manifest_sha256: @delivery.manifest_sha256,
            source_sha256: @delivery.source_sha256, mapping_sha256: @mapping.sha256,
            preview_sha256: plan.sha256, binding_json: self.class.json(plan.binding))
          retained = Digest::SHA256.new
          plan.each_entry { |entry| retained.update(self.class.json(apply_entry(entry, edition)) + "\n") }
          result = {"schema"=>SCHEMA, "stream_id"=>@stream.id.to_s, "edition_id"=>edition.id.to_s,
            "revision"=>revision, "operation_sha256"=>operation_sha,
            "manifest_sha256"=>@delivery.manifest_sha256, "source_sha256"=>@delivery.source_sha256,
            "mapping_sha256"=>@mapping.sha256, "preview_sha256"=>plan.sha256,
            "preview_entries_sha256"=>plan.entries_sha256, "retained_entries_sha256"=>retained.hexdigest,
            "binding"=>plan.binding, "counts"=>plan.counts, "entry_count"=>plan.row_count,
            "committed_at"=>Time.now.utc.iso8601(6)}
          raw = self.class.json(result)
          edition.update!(receipt_json: raw, receipt_sha256: self.class.sha(raw))
          @stream.update!(revision: revision, latest_edition_id: edition.id, target_model: @model.name,
            scope_sha256: @scope_sha, key_mapping_sha256: @mapping.key_sha256, membership_sha256: @membership_sha)
          @stream.reload
          self.class.need(@stream.revision == revision && @stream.latest_edition_id == edition.id,
            "DATASET_STREAM_WRITE_CHANGED")
          validate_stream!
          self.class.need(verified_receipt(edition.reload) == result, "DATASET_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
        end
      end
      self.class.need(result, "DATASET_IMPORT_ROLLED_BACK")
      result
    ensure
      plan&.close
    end

    # Full original edition export can be reopened independently of the current
    # source edition. Customer records and their source rows remain on the same
    # transaction history, including removed keys and exact original JSON lines.
    def write_receipt(io, operation_key:)
      operation_sha = operation_identity(operation_key)
      edition = @models[:edition].find_by(dataset_stream_id: @stream.id, operation_sha256: operation_sha)
      self.class.need(edition, "DATASET_RECEIPT_MISSING")
      validate_stream!
      selected = verified_receipt(edition)
      io.write(self.class.json(selected).delete_suffix("}") + ',"rows":[')
      first, digest, count = true, Digest::SHA256.new, 0
      @models[:entry].where(dataset_edition_id: edition.id).find_each do |entry|
        raw = entry.record_json
        self.class.need(self.class.sha(raw) == entry.record_sha256, "DATASET_EDITION_ROW_CHANGED")
        digest.update(raw + "\n")
        io.write(",") unless first
        io.write(raw)
        first = false
        count += 1
      end
      self.class.need(count == selected["entry_count"] &&
        digest.hexdigest == selected["retained_entries_sha256"], "DATASET_EDITION_ROWS_CHANGED")
      io.write("]}\n")
      selected
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
# MIT. Durable business-job receiving over the original seller and Node Buyer.
require_relative "seller_client"

module Starforge
  # Keep the key in your application's job/database record. The same key selects
  # one native intent across Active Job retries and process restarts.
  class Receiving
    attr_reader :directory, :intent_id
    def self.key_id(key)
      Files.need(key.is_a?(String) && !key.strip.empty? && key.bytesize <= 1024 &&
        key.valid_encoding?, "RUBY_BUSINESS_KEY_REQUIRED")
      Files.hash(key.b)
    end
    def self.intent_id(key)
      "ruby:" + key_id(key)
    end
    def self.received(directory:, key:, expected_manifest_sha256: nil)
      root = Files.directory(directory)
      path = Files.directory(File.join(root,key_id(key)))
      job_bytes = Files.read(File.join(path,"job.json"),131_072)
      job = Files.parse(job_bytes)
      receipt = Files.parse(Files.read(File.join(path,"received.json"),131_072))
      Files.need(job["schema"] == "stellar-forge.ruby-business-job.v1" &&
        job["keySha256"] == key_id(key) && job["intentId"] == intent_id(key) &&
        receipt["schema"] == "stellar-forge.ruby-business-received.v1" &&
        receipt["jobSha256"] == Files.hash(job_bytes) &&
        receipt["intentId"] == job["intentId"] && receipt["sourceSha256"] == job["sourceSha256"] &&
        receipt["directory"] == File.join(path,"received"), "RUBY_BUSINESS_RECEIPT_CHANGED")
      Files.need(expected_manifest_sha256.nil? || receipt["manifestSha256"] == expected_manifest_sha256,
        "RUBY_DELIVERY_MANIFEST_CHANGED")
      delivery = Delivery.open(receipt["directory"],expected_manifest_sha256: receipt.fetch("manifestSha256"))
      Files.need(delivery.manifest["intentId"] == job["intentId"] &&
        delivery.manifest["sourceSha256"] == job["sourceSha256"], "RUBY_BUSINESS_DELIVERY_CHANGED")
      delivery
    end

    def initialize(client:, buyer:, directory:, key:, bound:, response_file: nil)
      Files.need(client.is_a?(SellerClient) && buyer.is_a?(Buyer) && bound.is_a?(BoundRequest),
        "RUBY_BUSINESS_SOURCE_REQUIRED")
      @client, @buyer, @key = client, buyer, key.dup.freeze
      @root = Files.directory(directory,create: true)
      @directory = Files.directory(File.join(@root,self.class.key_id(key)),create: true)
      @intent_id = self.class.intent_id(key)
      Files.need(bound.intent_id == @intent_id && bound.source_sha256 == client.source["sourceSha256"],
        "RUBY_BUSINESS_INTENT_CHANGED")
      Files.need(response_file.nil? || response_file.is_a?(Hash), "RUBY_RESPONSE_OPTIONS_REQUIRED")
      @response_file = response_file.nil? ? nil : Files.parse(Files.json(Files.values!(response_file)))
      @bound = bound
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        bound.save(File.join(@directory,"request"))
        plan = Files.read(File.join(@directory,"request","request-plan.json"),131_072)
        job = {"schema"=>"stellar-forge.ruby-business-job.v1","keySha256"=>self.class.key_id(key),
          "intentId"=>@intent_id,"buyerDirectory"=>buyer.directory,"sourceSha256"=>bound.source_sha256,
          "rubyManifestSha256"=>client.manifest_sha256,"requestPlanSha256"=>Files.hash(plan),
          "requestSha256"=>Files.hash(bound.record_bytes),"responseFile"=>@response_file}
        @job_bytes = Files.json(job).freeze
        @job_sha = Files.hash(@job_bytes)
        Files.once(File.join(@directory,"job.json"),@job_bytes)
      end
    end

    def bound
      @client.load_request(File.join(@directory,"request"))
    end
    def operation
      Operation.new(@buyer,@intent_id,@bound.source_sha256)
    end
    def same_job!
      Files.need(Files.read(File.join(@directory,"job.json"),131_072) == @job_bytes,
        "RUBY_BUSINESS_JOB_CHANGED")
    end
    def complete?
      File.file?(File.join(@directory,"received.json"))
    end
    def delivery
      self.class.received(directory: @root,key: @key)
    end

    # Repeating preparation adopts the exact existing native operation. The
    # original native intent and bound request, not a transport UUID, own it.
    def prepare(cancel: nil)
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        same_job!
        prepare_inside(cancel: cancel)
      end
    end
    def prepare_inside(cancel: nil)
      path = File.join(@directory,"prepared.json")
      if File.exist?(path)
        saved = Files.parse(Files.read(path,131_072))
        Files.need(saved["jobSha256"] == @job_sha && saved["intentId"] == @intent_id,
          "RUBY_BUSINESS_PREPARATION_CHANGED")
        return operation
      end
      selected = bound
      prepared = @client.prepare(@buyer,selected,response_file: @response_file,cancel: cancel)
      Files.once(path,Files.json({"schema"=>"stellar-forge.ruby-business-prepared.v1",
        "jobSha256"=>@job_sha,"intentId"=>@intent_id}))
      prepared
    end
    private :prepare_inside

    def review(cancel: nil)
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        same_job!
        selected = prepare_inside(cancel: cancel)
        path = File.join(@directory,"review.json")
        if File.exist?(path)
          saved = Files.parse(Files.read(path))
          Files.need(saved["intentId"] == @intent_id, "RUBY_BUSINESS_REVIEW_CHANGED")
          return saved
        end
        value = selected.review(cancel: cancel)
        Files.once(path,Files.json(value))
        value
      end
    end

    # Call only from the explicit operator action. A worker retry uses recover
    # and receive; it never grants a new paid attempt.
    def execute(review:, cancel: nil)
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        same_job!
        review_bytes = Files.read(File.join(@directory,"review.json"))
        Files.need(Files.parse(review_bytes) == review && review["intentId"] == @intent_id,
          "RUBY_BUSINESS_REVIEW_CHANGED")
        path = File.join(@directory,"execution.json")
        plan = if File.exist?(path)
          Files.parse(Files.read(path,131_072))
        else
          value = {"schema"=>"stellar-forge.ruby-business-execution.v1",
            "jobSha256"=>@job_sha,"intentId"=>@intent_id,"reviewSha256"=>Files.hash(review_bytes),
            "callId"=>SecureRandom.uuid}
          Files.once(path,Files.json(value))
          value
        end
        Files.need(plan["jobSha256"] == @job_sha && plan["intentId"] == @intent_id &&
          plan["reviewSha256"] == Files.hash(review_bytes) && CALL_ID.match?(plan["callId"] || ""),
          "RUBY_BUSINESS_EXECUTION_CHANGED")
        begin
          operation.execute(review: review,call_id: plan["callId"],cancel: cancel)
        rescue Error => cause
          # Reading an original result is safe after a lost native reply. A null
          # recovery preserves the actual original error for the operator.
          recovered = operation.recover(cancel: cancel) unless cancel&.cancelled?
          raise cause if recovered.nil?
          recovered
        end
      end
    end

    def recover(cancel: nil)
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        same_job!
        operation.recover(cancel: cancel)
      end
    end
    def status(cancel: nil)
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        same_job!
        return {"state"=>"RECEIVED","intentId"=>@intent_id,"delivery"=>delivery.manifest} if complete?
        {"state"=>File.exist?(File.join(@directory,"execution.json")) ? "ORIGINAL_ATTEMPT" :
          File.exist?(File.join(@directory,"prepared.json")) ? "PREPARED" : "REQUEST_RETAINED",
          "intentId"=>@intent_id,"operation"=>File.exist?(File.join(@directory,"prepared.json")) ?
            operation.status(cancel: cancel) : nil}
      end
    end

    def receive(cancel: nil)
      Files.lock(@directory) do
        same_job!
        return delivery if complete?
        result = operation.recover(cancel: cancel)
        Files.need(result && result.dig("delivery","status") == "SAVED", "RUBY_ORIGINAL_RESPONSE_REQUIRED")
        received = operation.receive(File.join(@directory,"received"),cancel: cancel)
        Files.once(File.join(@directory,"received.json"),Files.json({
          "schema"=>"stellar-forge.ruby-business-received.v1","jobSha256"=>@job_sha,
          "intentId"=>@intent_id,"sourceSha256"=>@bound.source_sha256,
          "directory"=>received.directory,"manifestSha256"=>received.manifest_sha256}))
        received
      end
    end
  end
end

# Ruby and Rails customer applications

A seller can deliver its current OpenAPI contract as a complete Ruby customer package. The application constructs the selected request with the generated seller implementation, prepares it through the installed Node Buyer, reviews its exact terms and body, executes through the existing operator, and receives a complete response that can be reopened offline.

The package also includes a durable receiving service for Rails jobs. A stable business key selects one native intent. The application can restart, recover the same operation, import its complete saved response, and resume database processing without requesting another purchase.

For complete paginated datasets, use [Dataset receiving and Rails editions](DATASETS.md). That workflow retains the original native acquisition, receives every SF100 data file, previews all mapped row changes and commits the selected edition with its application receipt. The complete migration, models, job and commissioning command are delivered in [examples/rails_dataset](examples/rails_dataset/README.md).

For a completed SF100 room already retained by its source owner, [direct native receiving](NATIVE_DATASETS.md) provides the original Python/Node scan, exact portable Ruby data packet, and a complete independently movable Rails application delivery. It shares the same row, meaning, receipt and edition APIs and can be exported as a standalone sixteen-file customer package.

## Create and deliver the customer package

Use the current seller OpenAPI exported by the maintained merchant workspace:

~~~sh
starforge client ruby export --openapi /absolute/seller-openapi.json --out /absolute/customer-package
starforge client ruby status --dir /absolute/customer-package
~~~

The same command is available directly from this source:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/developer/ruby-client/export.mjs \
  export --openapi /absolute/seller-openapi.json --out /absolute/customer-package
~~~

An already completed JavaScript customer export can receive its Ruby companions with:

~~~sh
starforge client ruby resume --dir /absolute/existing-customer-export
~~~

The exporter preserves the original five JavaScript files and their existing client-export.json. The current edition adds 26 Ruby/application files and writes ruby-client.json after every companion is complete. Each file carries an exact byte count and SHA-256. The Ruby manifest also binds the original client-export.json and seller source hash.

| File | Purpose |

Inspection and copy preserve existing complete eight-file and twenty-one-file Ruby editions. Export to a new destination for the current full Dataset/Rails edition; completed existing packages retain their original manifests. The current exporter includes and verifies every nested Rails example file.

Use exact-copy delivery when transferring an existing package:

~~~sh
starforge client ruby copy --dir /absolute/customer-package --out /absolute/recipient-package
starforge client ruby copy-resume --dir /absolute/customer-package --out /absolute/interrupted-recipient
~~~

Copy and copy-resume retain the selected bytes and original manifests. Additive resume completes an interrupted export from the matching source; a conflicting companion file requires its existing source version or a new destination. Keep the completed package with the customer application so a later seller deployment does not change an existing job's contract.

## Runtime and host selection

Use Linux, Ruby 3.1 or newer with JSON, BigDecimal, CSV and the other standard libraries used by seller_client.rb, and the installed Node 24 SF88 buyer runtime. Preparation and execution load that runtime's node/index.mjs and CLI from the host-selected directory. The customer package contains application adapters; the native operator, signing integration, policy, wallet, HTTP transport, reconciliation and ledger come from that existing installation.

Each application selects a private buyer state directory. The same state directory and intent reopen the same operation. Select either an existing operator profile or an initialized native buyer workspace. The workspace route preserves its own configuration and operator identity.

~~~ruby
require_relative "customer-package/rails_receiving"

client = Starforge::SellerClient.new("/absolute/customer-package")
buyer = Starforge::Buyer.new(
  client: client,
  runtime_directory: "/absolute/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli",
  state_directory: "/absolute/private/ruby-buyer",
  workspace_directory: "/absolute/private/original-buyer-workspace"
)
~~~

For a profile-based customer, replace workspace_directory with operator_profile pointing to the original private profile JSON. Host environment variables remain available to the original signing and approval integrations. The adapter removes Node runtime injection variables NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH. It preserves the host's original stdin and existing approval-broker environment for the native operator; approval continues in that original terminal or browser session.

Call buyer.close during application or worker shutdown. It closes admission, cancels active child calls, and waits for their cleanup. Request generation uses a finite JSON input; payment and receiving calls use private files and the original Node child lifecycle. Each call has a timeout, a private process result, and a durable response. A process cancellation leaves the original buyer's recorded attempt available for recovery.

## Select a real operation and retain its request

Inspect the delivered contract before selecting an operation:

~~~sh
ruby /absolute/customer-package/customer.rb contract --package /absolute/customer-package
~~~

In Ruby, client.operations returns the exact operation descriptions and payment choices. Select the actual operation ID, path/query inputs, payment alternative and atomic ceiling from that contract.

~~~ruby
key = "monthly-source-refresh:account-42:2026-10"
bound = client.build_request(
  ENV.fetch("SELLER_OPERATION_ID"),
  {
    "path" => JSON.parse(File.read("/absolute/private/path-inputs.json")),
    "query" => JSON.parse(File.read("/absolute/private/query-inputs.json"))
  },
  intent_id: Starforge::Receiving.intent_id(key),
  max_atomic: ENV.fetch("SELECTED_MAX_ATOMIC"),
  accept_index: Integer(ENV.fetch("SELECTED_ACCEPT_INDEX"))
)
bound.save("/absolute/private/retained-request")
~~~

Require rails_receiving.rb before using Receiving.intent_id. A plain Ruby application can instead choose its own stable intent string and use seller_client.rb directly.

## Prepare, review, execute and recover

The direct API exposes the existing original buyer operation:

~~~ruby
begin
  operation = client.prepare(buyer, bound)
  review = operation.review
  # Present and inspect this actual native review in the existing operator flow.
  result = operation.execute(review: review)
  puts result.fetch("status")
ensure
  buyer.close
end
~~~

execute requires the selected review. The native operator still performs its own approval and policy checks. Keep this call in the actual operator session, with its original terminal or scoped browser approval integration. Background receiving jobs use recover and receive.

Operation.status returns its native state, delivery status, retry guidance and bound seller source. Operation.recover reads the same saved result and original native output. It returns nil when that operation has no recoverable result. A recoverable transport result preserves the native status, exit information, runtime error, response descriptor and stream metadata.

Each application call has a UUID separate from the purchase intent. Pass call_id when the application already retains a transport request ID. Repeating that UUID returns its saved response or reports the original unavailable reply. It does not blindly repeat a dispatched child. The original buyer's create-only attempt record independently preserves the same purchase across Ruby and Node restarts.

A new call ID is appropriate for a fresh read of evolving status or recovery. Repeating a preparation with the same exact bound request adopts an existing matching prepared operation. Repeating an execution still reaches the original single-attempt protection. Preserve an incomplete native preparation and its original state if the native runtime reports that it needs recovery.

## Receive complete data and reopen offline

After the original result contains a SAVED response, receive it into a private directory:

~~~ruby
operation = client.reopen(buyer, bound.intent_id)
delivery = operation.receive("/absolute/private/customer-receipt")
expected_manifest = delivery.manifest_sha256
~~~

Receiving copies the saved response through the existing Node result.verify and result.saveAs implementation. It retains the selected source, request, body when present, review, native result and complete response.bin. A saved receiving plan binds those files before copying, so interrupted recovery uses the same selected result. customer-delivery.json completes the handoff.

The response's native status remains in result.json. A saved response may be an application error response; inspect its original status and runtime information before applying business changes.

A later process can reopen without Node or network:

~~~ruby
require_relative "customer-package/seller_client"

delivery = Starforge::Delivery.open(
  "/absolute/private/customer-receipt",
  expected_manifest_sha256: expected_manifest
)
data = delivery.json
~~~

Delivery.open verifies every complete file, the selected manifest and source/request/review/result bindings. Each data reader uses a complete private snapshot whose SHA-256 is checked before application code receives bytes. This keeps database callbacks from acting on a response that fails its final digest.

Use delivery.bytes for a bounded binary response, each_chunk for streaming, json for JSON, and each_csv for CSV. JSON response integers retain Ruby precision and decimal values use BigDecimal. CSV with headers returns CSV::Row, retaining duplicate column names and their original order. Select fields according to the actual delivered schema.

~~~ruby
delivery.each_csv do |row|
  original_fields = row.fields
  original_headers = row.headers
  # Apply the project's explicit field mapping here.
end
~~~

Receiving artifacts are private application data. Preserve the expected manifest hash in the application's job/database record when transferring a handoff to another machine.

## Rails service and Active Job integration

rails_receiving.rb is framework independent. It can be called from a Rails service, job or console without adding a second queue. The business key should come from a persisted model identity and edition, such as a source-import row's UUID. Keep that key unchanged across framework retries.

~~~ruby
require Rails.root.join("vendor", "seller-package", "rails_receiving").to_s

class SellerImport
  def self.open(import)
    client = Starforge::SellerClient.new(import.package_directory)
    buyer = Starforge::Buyer.new(
      client: client,
      runtime_directory: import.runtime_directory,
      state_directory: import.buyer_directory,
      workspace_directory: import.original_workspace_directory
    )
    bound = client.load_request(import.request_directory)
    service = Starforge::Receiving.new(
      client: client,
      buyer: buyer,
      directory: import.jobs_directory,
      key: import.business_key,
      bound: bound,
      response_file: import.response_options
    )
    yield service
  ensure
    buyer&.close
  end
end
~~~

The fields in this service belong to your existing model. Store the actual selected host, package and request paths at import creation. Build and save that request with Receiving.intent_id(import.business_key), so the service can bind it to the same job.

An operator prepares and reviews the source import, then executes through the existing native operator session. The service retains one execution UUID before dispatch and verifies the saved review on repeat. A lost response is recovered from the original buyer.

~~~ruby
SellerImport.open(import) do |service|
  review = service.review
  # Existing operator UI/terminal presents this review.
  service.execute(review: review)
end
ReceiveSellerImportJob.perform_later(import.id)
~~~

The job receives and applies the resulting data. The example below illustrates one transaction and a retained manifest check; use your project's actual schema and uniqueness key.

~~~ruby
class ReceiveSellerImportJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :source_imports

  def perform(import_id)
    import = SourceImport.find(import_id)
    delivery = nil
    SellerImport.open(import) { |service| delivery = service.receive }
    payload = delivery.json

    import.with_lock do
      if import.received_manifest_sha256.present?
        raise "Different source receipt" unless
          import.received_manifest_sha256 == delivery.manifest_sha256
        return
      end
      SourceImport.transaction do
        # The existing domain service validates the real payload and uses its
        # actual unique source identifiers for inserts/updates.
        SourceImportApplier.call(import, payload)
        import.update!(
          received_manifest_sha256: delivery.manifest_sha256,
          received_directory: delivery.directory,
          received_at: Time.current
        )
      end
    end
  end
end
~~~

The domain apply and receipt update occur in the same database transaction. A retry after commit finds the original manifest and returns. A retry before commit reuses the same saved response. File receiving is complete before that transaction starts, keeping network/process lifetime outside the database lock.

Classify service errors in the existing application queue. An unfinished original response can be reviewed or recovered; changed source/request/receipt identities require resolving that original selection. Ordinary framework retry configuration applies to receiving and domain writes. Rails documents retry_on, discard_on and transaction behavior in its [Active Job guide](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_job_basics.html).

      Files.need(Files.read(File.join(@directory,"ruby-client.json"),131_072) == @manifest_bytes &&
        @manifest["schema"] == "stellar-forge.ruby-seller-client.v1", "RUBY_PACKAGE_CHANGED")
      base_bytes = Files.read(File.join(@directory,"client-export.json"),131_072)
      base = Files.parse(base_bytes)
      Files.need(Files.hash(base_bytes) == @manifest["originalManifestSha256"] &&
        base["sourceSha256"] == @manifest["sourceSha256"], "RUBY_ORIGINAL_EXPORT_CHANGED")
      selected = [LEGACY_RUBY_FILES,LEGACY_DATASET_RUBY_FILES,LEGACY_COMPLETE_RUBY_FILES,RUBY_FILES].find { |files|
        @manifest["files"].is_a?(Array) && @manifest["files"].length == files.length
      }
      Files.need(selected, "RUBY_PACKAGE_INCOMPLETE")
      [[ORIGINAL_FILES,base["files"]],[selected,@manifest["files"]]].each do |names,entries|
        Files.need(entries.is_a?(Array) && entries.map { |item| item["name"] } == names, "RUBY_PACKAGE_INCOMPLETE")
        entries.each do |entry|
          path = File.join(@directory,entry.fetch("name"))
          Files.directory(File.dirname(path),private: false)
          raw = Files.read(path)
          Files.need(entry["bytes"].is_a?(Integer) && raw.bytesize == entry["bytes"] &&
            Files.hash(raw) == entry["sha256"], "RUBY_PACKAGE_FILE_CHANGED")
        end
      end
      true
    end
    def dataset_available?
      verify_package!
      @manifest["files"].any? { |entry| entry["name"] == "seller-dataset-bridge.mjs" }
    end
    def native_dataset_available?
      verify_package!
      @manifest["files"].any? { |entry| entry["name"] == "native_dataset.rb" }
    end
    def source
      Files.parse(Files.json(@snapshot.slice("schema","sourceSha256","mode","title","origin")))
    end
    def operations
      Files.parse(Files.json(@snapshot.fetch("operations")))
    end
    def build_request(operation_id, inputs, intent_id:, max_atomic:, accept_index: nil, payment_flow: nil)
      Files.need(inputs.is_a?(Hash), "RUBY_REQUEST_INPUTS_REQUIRED")
      selected = inputs.dup
      if selected.key?("multipart")
        part = selected["multipart"]
        Files.need(part.is_a?(Hash) && part.keys.sort == %w[body contentType] &&
          part["body"].is_a?(String) && part["body"].bytesize <= MAX_BODY, "RUBY_MULTIPART_BYTES_REQUIRED")
        selected["multipart"] = {"bodyBase64"=>Base64.strict_encode64(part["body"].b), "contentType"=>part["contentType"]}
      end
      auth = {"intentId"=>intent_id,"maxAtomic"=>max_atomic}
      auth["acceptIndex"] = accept_index unless accept_index.nil?
      auth["paymentFlow"] = payment_flow unless payment_flow.nil?
      payload = {"sourceSha256"=>source.fetch("sourceSha256"),"operationId"=>operation_id,"inputs"=>selected,"authorization"=>auth}
      Files.values!(payload)
      build(Files.json(payload))
    end
    def build(payload)
      verify_package!
      Files.need(payload.is_a?(String) && payload.bytesize <= MAX_INPUT, "RUBY_REQUEST_INPUT_LIMIT")
      Files.values!(Files.parse(payload))
      run = @runner.run(File.join(@directory,"seller-client-bridge.mjs"),input: payload,timeout: @timeout)
      raise Error, run[:error] if run[:error]
      unless run[:status].success?
        raise Error, "RUBY_ORIGINAL_REQUEST_REJECTED"
      end
      result, supplied = Files.parse(run[:stdout]), Files.parse(payload)
      Files.need(result["schema"] == "stellar-forge.ruby-seller-request.v1" &&
        result["sourceSha256"] == source["sourceSha256"] && result["operationId"] == supplied["operationId"],
        "RUBY_REQUEST_SOURCE_CHANGED")
      body = nil
      unless result["body"].nil?
        descriptor = result["body"]
        encoded = descriptor.delete("base64")
        begin
          body = Base64.strict_decode64(encoded)
        rescue ArgumentError, TypeError
          raise Error, "RUBY_REQUEST_BODY_CHANGED"
        end
        Files.need(body.bytesize <= MAX_BODY && body.bytesize == descriptor["bytes"] &&
          Files.hash(body) == descriptor["sha256"] && Base64.strict_encode64(body) == encoded, "RUBY_REQUEST_BODY_CHANGED")
      end
      result["inputSha256"] = Files.hash(payload)
      result["originalManifestSha256"] = @manifest.fetch("originalManifestSha256")
      result["rubyManifestSha256"] = @manifest_sha256
      verify_package!
      BoundRequest.new(payload,Files.json(result),body)
    end
    def load_request(directory)
      directory = Files.directory(directory)
      manifest = Files.parse(Files.read(File.join(directory,"request-plan.json"),131_072))
      Files.need(manifest["schema"] == "stellar-forge.ruby-seller-request-plan.v1" &&
        manifest["sourceSha256"] == source["sourceSha256"], "RUBY_REQUEST_PLAN_CHANGED")
      entries = manifest["files"]
      Files.need(entries.is_a?(Array) &&
        [%w[request-input.json request.json],%w[request-input.json request.json request.body]].include?(entries.map { |f| f["name"] }),
        "RUBY_REQUEST_PLAN_INCOMPLETE")
      saved = {}
      entries.each do |entry|
        raw = Files.read(File.join(directory,entry["name"]))
        Files.need(raw.bytesize == entry["bytes"] && Files.hash(raw) == entry["sha256"], "RUBY_REQUEST_PLAN_CHANGED")
        saved[entry["name"]] = raw
      end
      Files.values!(Files.parse(saved.fetch("request-input.json")))
      rebuilt = build(saved.fetch("request-input.json"))
      Files.need(rebuilt.record_bytes == saved["request.json"] && rebuilt.body == saved["request.body"], "RUBY_REQUEST_PLAN_CHANGED")
      rebuilt
    end
    def prepare(buyer, bound, response_file: nil, call_id: nil, cancel: nil)
      Files.need(bound.is_a?(BoundRequest) && buyer.is_a?(Buyer), "RUBY_BOUND_REQUEST_REQUIRED")
      Files.need(buyer.client_manifest_sha256 == @manifest_sha256, "RUBY_BUYER_PACKAGE_CHANGED")
      rebuilt = build(bound.input_bytes)
      Files.need(rebuilt.record_bytes == bound.record_bytes && rebuilt.body == bound.body, "RUBY_BOUND_REQUEST_CHANGED")
      record = bound.describe
      record["bodyBase64"] = Base64.strict_encode64(bound.body) unless bound.body.nil?
      arguments = {"bound"=>record}
      arguments["responseFile"] = response_file unless response_file.nil?
      buyer.invoke("prepare", bound.intent_id, arguments, call_id: call_id, cancel: cancel)
      Operation.new(buyer, bound.intent_id, source.fetch("sourceSha256"))
    end
    def reopen(buyer, intent_id)
      operation = Operation.new(buyer,intent_id,source.fetch("sourceSha256"))
      operation.status
      operation
    end

  class Buyer
    attr_reader :directory, :client_manifest_sha256
    def initialize(client:, runtime_directory:, state_directory:, node: "node", environment: nil,
      operator_profile: nil, workspace_directory: nil, timeout: 420, output_limit: 16_777_216)
      Files.need(client.is_a?(SellerClient), "RUBY_SELLER_CLIENT_REQUIRED")
      Files.need(timeout.is_a?(Numeric) && timeout.finite? && timeout > 35 && timeout <= 7200, "RUBY_TIMEOUT_INVALID")
      Files.need(output_limit.is_a?(Integer) && output_limit.between?(65_536,MAX_INPUT), "RUBY_OUTPUT_LIMIT_INVALID")
      @client, @timeout, @output_limit = client, timeout, output_limit
      @client_manifest_sha256 = client.manifest_sha256.dup.freeze
      @directory = Files.directory(state_directory,create: true)
      @calls = Files.directory(File.join(@directory,"ruby-calls"),create: true)
      @runtime = {"runtimeDirectory"=>File.realpath(runtime_directory.to_s),"stateDirectory"=>@directory,
        "timeoutMs"=>([timeout - 35,1].max * 1000).to_i,"outputLimit"=>output_limit}
      @runtime["operatorProfile"] = File.realpath(operator_profile.to_s) unless operator_profile.nil?
      @runtime["workspaceDirectory"] = File.realpath(workspace_directory.to_s) unless workspace_directory.nil?
      Files.need(operator_profile.nil? || workspace_directory.nil?, "RUBY_SELECT_ONE_OPERATOR_SOURCE")
      @runner = Runner.new(node: node,environment: environment)
      @mutex, @condition, @active, @closing = Mutex.new, ConditionVariable.new, {}, false
    end
    def invoke(action, intent_id = nil, arguments = {}, call_id: nil, cancel: nil)
      call_id ||= SecureRandom.uuid
      Files.need(CALL_ID.match?(call_id) && (intent_id.nil? || INTENT.match?(intent_id)), "RUBY_OPERATION_ID_REQUIRED")
      token = cancel || Cancellation.new
      invocation = Object.new
      @mutex.synchronize do
        raise Error, "RUBY_BUYER_CLOSING" if @closing
        @active[invocation] = token
      end
      begin
        @client.verify_package!
        scope = Files.directory(File.join(@calls,call_id),create: true)
        request = {"schema"=>"stellar-forge.ruby-buyer-call.v1","callId"=>call_id,"action"=>action,
          "id"=>intent_id,"runtime"=>@runtime,"arguments"=>arguments}
        raw = Files.json(Files.values!(request))
        Files.need(raw.bytesize <= MAX_INPUT, "RUBY_CALL_SIZE_LIMIT")
        Files.lock(scope) do
          Files.once(File.join(scope,"request.json"),raw)
          response = File.join(scope,"response.json")
          unless File.exist?(response)
            marker = File.join(scope,"dispatch.json")
            if File.exist?(marker)
              raise Error.new("RUBY_NATIVE_REPLY_UNAVAILABLE_USE_RECOVER",call_id: call_id,intent_id: intent_id)
            end
            dataset_call = action.start_with?("dataset.")
            Files.need(!dataset_call || @client.dataset_available?, "RUBY_DATASET_PACKAGE_REQUIRED")
            bridge = dataset_call ? "seller-dataset-bridge.mjs" : "seller-buyer-bridge.mjs"
            Files.once(marker,Files.json({"requestSha256"=>Files.hash(raw),"callId"=>call_id}))
            run = @runner.run(File.join(@client.directory,bridge),
              [File.join(scope,"request.json")],timeout: @timeout,limit: @output_limit,cancel: token,inherit_stdin: true)
            Files.once(File.join(scope,"process.json"),Files.json({"exitCode"=>run[:status].exitstatus,
              "signal"=>run[:status].termsig,"error"=>run[:error]}))
            unless File.exist?(response)
              raise Error.new(run[:error] || "RUBY_NATIVE_REPLY_UNAVAILABLE_USE_RECOVER",call_id: call_id,intent_id: intent_id)
            end
          end
          value = Files.parse(Files.read(response,MAX_INPUT))
          Files.need(value["schema"] == request["schema"] && value["callId"] == call_id &&
            value["action"] == action && value["id"] == intent_id, "RUBY_NATIVE_REPLY_CHANGED")
          unless value["ok"] == true
            code = value.dig("error","code")
            code = "RUBY_NATIVE_OPERATION_FAILED" unless code.is_a?(String) && /\A[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,119}\z/.match?(code)
            raise Error.new(code,call_id: call_id,intent_id: intent_id)
          end
          value["result"]
        end
      ensure
        @mutex.synchronize { @active.delete(invocation); @condition.broadcast }
      end
    end
    def ready
      invoke("ready")
    end
    def close
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @closing = true
        @active.each_value(&:cancel)
        @condition.wait(@mutex) until @active.empty?
      end
      nil
    end
  end

  class Operation
    attr_reader :buyer, :intent_id, :source_sha256
    def initialize(buyer,intent_id,source_sha256)
      Files.need(INTENT.match?(intent_id) && HASH.match?(source_sha256), "RUBY_OPERATION_SELECTION_REQUIRED")
      @buyer,@intent_id,@source_sha256 = buyer,intent_id.dup.freeze,source_sha256.dup.freeze
    end
    def call(action, arguments = {}, **options)
      @buyer.invoke(action,@intent_id,{"sourceSha256"=>@source_sha256}.merge(arguments),**options)
    end
    def status(**options)
      call("inspect",{},**options)
    end
    def inspect
      "#<Starforge::Operation intent_id=#{@intent_id}>"
    end
    def review(**options)
      call("review",{},**options)
    end
    def execute(review:, **options)
      call("execute",{"review"=>review},**options)
    end
    def recover(**options)

    end
    def receive(directory, **options)
      result = call("receive",{"directory"=>File.expand_path(directory.to_s)},**options)
      Delivery.open(result.fetch("directory"),expected_manifest_sha256: result.fetch("manifestSha256"))
    end
  end

  # Receiving is complete before application code sees any data. Reopening uses
  # the original packet and response hashes and needs no Node process or network.
  class Delivery
    attr_reader :directory, :manifest_sha256
    def self.open(directory, expected_manifest_sha256:)
      new(directory,expected_manifest_sha256: expected_manifest_sha256)
    end
    def initialize(directory, expected_manifest_sha256:)
      @directory = Files.directory(directory)
      Files.need(HASH.match?(expected_manifest_sha256), "RUBY_DELIVERY_MANIFEST_REQUIRED")
      @manifest_sha256 = expected_manifest_sha256
      bytes = Files.read(File.join(@directory,"customer-delivery.json"),131_072)
      Files.need(Files.hash(bytes) == @manifest_sha256, "RUBY_DELIVERY_MANIFEST_CHANGED")
      @manifest = Files.parse(bytes)
      entries = @manifest["files"]
      names = entries.is_a?(Array) ? entries.map { |entry| entry["name"] } : []
      Files.need(@manifest["schema"] == "stellar-forge.ruby-customer-delivery.v1" &&
        INTENT.match?(@manifest["intentId"] || "") && HASH.match?(@manifest["sourceSha256"] || "") &&
        HASH.match?(@manifest["configSha256"] || "") && HASH.match?(@manifest["responseSha256"] || "") &&
        names.uniq == names && names.length.between?(5,6) &&
        %w[source.json request.json review.json result.json response.bin].all? { |name| names.include?(name) } &&
        (names - %w[source.json request.json request.body review.json result.json response.bin]).empty?,
        "RUBY_DELIVERY_MANIFEST_INVALID")
      entries.each do |entry|
        Files.need(entry["bytes"].is_a?(Integer) && entry["bytes"] >= 0 && entry["bytes"] <= 1_073_741_824 &&
          HASH.match?(entry["sha256"] || ""), "RUBY_DELIVERY_FILE_INVALID")
        with_snapshot(entry.fetch("name")) { |_file| }
      end
      Files.need(descriptor("response.bin")["sha256"] == @manifest["responseSha256"], "RUBY_DELIVERY_RESPONSE_CHANGED")
      source = json_file("source.json")
      request = json_file("request.json")
      review = json_file("review.json")
      native = json_file("result.json")
      Files.need(source["sourceSha256"] == @manifest["sourceSha256"] && source["request"] == request &&
        request["intentId"] == @manifest["intentId"] && source["configSha256"] == @manifest["configSha256"] &&
        review["intentId"] == @manifest["intentId"] && review["configSha256"] == @manifest["configSha256"] &&
        native["intentId"] == @manifest["intentId"] && native["configSha256"] == @manifest["configSha256"],
        "RUBY_DELIVERY_SOURCE_CHANGED")
    end
    def manifest
      Files.parse(Files.json(@manifest))
    end
    def descriptor(name)
      entry = @manifest.fetch("files").find { |item| item["name"] == name }
      Files.need(entry, "RUBY_DELIVERY_FILE_UNKNOWN")
      entry.dup
    end
    def with_snapshot(name)
      entry = descriptor(name)
      source = File.open(File.join(@directory,name),File::RDONLY | File::NOFOLLOW | File::NONBLOCK)
      tmp = Tempfile.new([".starforge-receive-",".bin"])
      begin
        tmp.binmode
        tmp.unlink
        before = source.stat
        Files.need(before.file? && before.size == entry["bytes"], "RUBY_DELIVERY_FILE_CHANGED")
        digest, count = Digest::SHA256.new, 0
        while (chunk = source.read(1_048_576))
          count += chunk.bytesize
          Files.need(count <= entry["bytes"], "RUBY_DELIVERY_FILE_CHANGED")
          digest.update(chunk)
          tmp.write(chunk)
        end
        after = source.stat
        Files.need(count == entry["bytes"] && digest.hexdigest == entry["sha256"] &&
          [before.dev,before.ino,before.size,before.mtime,before.ctime] ==
          [after.dev,after.ino,after.size,after.mtime,after.ctime], "RUBY_DELIVERY_FILE_CHANGED")
        tmp.flush
        tmp.rewind
        yield tmp
      ensure
        source.close
        tmp.close!
      end
    end
    def bytes(limit: 8_388_608)
      Files.need(descriptor("response.bin")["bytes"] <= limit, "RUBY_RESPONSE_LIMIT_USE_STREAM")
      with_snapshot("response.bin", &:read)
    end
    def each_chunk(chunk_size: 65_536)
      return enum_for(__method__,chunk_size: chunk_size) unless block_given?
      Files.need(chunk_size.is_a?(Integer) && chunk_size.between?(1,1_048_576), "RUBY_CHUNK_SIZE_INVALID")
      with_snapshot("response.bin") do |file|
        while (chunk = file.read(chunk_size))
          yield chunk
        end
      end
    end
    def json(limit: 67_108_864)
      Files.parse(bytes(limit: limit),decimals: true)
    end
    def json_file(name, limit: MAX_INPUT)
      Files.need(descriptor(name)["bytes"] <= limit, "RUBY_JSON_FILE_LIMIT")
      with_snapshot(name) { |file| Files.parse(file.read,decimals: true) }
    end
    def each_csv(headers: true)
      return enum_for(__method__,headers: headers) unless block_given?
      with_snapshot("response.bin") do |file|
        file.set_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8)
        CSV.new(file,headers: headers).each { |row| yield row }
      end
    end
  end
end

def main():
    a = options()
    if a.command == "binding":
        from managed import inspect_binding
        output(inspect_binding(a.workspace)); return
    if a.command == "serve" and a.expected_binding is not None:
        from managed import require_binding
        require_binding(a.workspace, a.expected_binding)
    with FeedWorkspace(a.workspace, create=a.command == "init") as ws:
        c = a.command
        if c == "serve":
            from server import OperatorServer
            if not 0 <= a.port <= 65535:
                raise InputError("Choose a port from 0 to 65535")
            binding = None
            if a.startup_format == "json" or a.expected_binding is not None:
                from managed import require_binding
                binding = require_binding(ws.root, a.expected_binding)
            server = OperatorServer(ws, a.port)
            previous = {}
            stopping = False
            def stop(signum, frame):
                nonlocal stopping
                ws.cancel_capture()
                if not stopping:
                    stopping = True
                    raise KeyboardInterrupt()
            try:
                for signum in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
                    previous[signum] = signal.signal(signum, stop)
                if a.startup_format == "json":
                    from managed import startup
                    server.launch = startup(server, binding, a.landing)
                    output(server.launch)
                else:
                    url = server.url if a.landing == "feeds" else server.origin + "/subscriptions#" + server.token
                    output({"console": url, "workspace": str(ws.root)})
                server.serve_forever(poll_interval=0.25)
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                pass
            finally:
                stopping = True
                ws.cancel_capture()
                server.server_close()
                server.join_worker()
                for signum, handler in previous.items():
                    signal.signal(signum, handler)
            return
        if c == "subscriptions":
            from subscriptions_cli import run_command
            result = run_command(ws, a, read_json, execute)
        elif c in ("init", "state"):
            result = ws.feed_state()
        elif c == "register":
            result = ws.register(a.feed, read_json(a.config), a.revision, a.operation)
        elif c == "capture":
            result = ws.capture(a.feed, a.operation, page_limit=a.pages, follow_pages=not a.one_page, force=a.force, from_capture=a.from_capture)
        elif c == "resume":
